Theme

Money, work & business

budget noun

also budgets, household budget, on a budget, within budget, over budget, make a budget

classical

Suet. Ner. 30.1: quibus impēnsārum ratiō cōnstāret, whose spending added up
Col. 4.5: quoniam impēnsārum ratiō modum postulat, since the reckoning of costs calls for a limit

ratiō impēnsārum

noun and genitive

the reckoning of expenses: a budget

No reference work gives a word for a budget; Latin reckons what is spent against what comes in. Cicero wanted his son’s spending fitted to the rents of two houses (sūmptūs … accommodet ad mercēdēs, Att. 12.32.2); to set a limit to spending is modum sūmptibus facere (Liv. 34.4).

Examples

  • Dīvitiārum et pecūniae frūctum nōn alium putābat quam profūsiōnem, sordidōs ac dēparcōs esse quibus impēnsārum ratiō cōnstāret

    He thought the only use of riches and money was to squander them, and that people whose spending added up were mean and stingySuet. Ner. 30.1

  • ut sūmptūs hujus peregrīnātiōnis … accommodet ad mercēdēs Argīlētī et Aventīnī

    that he should fit his spending while abroad to the rents from the Argiletum and the AventineCic. Att. 12.32.2

See also spend, save, income, economy, fund.
